contract.interface:
For a nonempty polytope P with vertices in{0,1}^n, let k(P) be maximum Hamming length of an actual edge, zero for a singleton. For every real m-by-n A with Euclidean column norms<=1 and every x in P, the source proposes x in conv{v vertex(P):||A(v-x)||infinity<=54k(P)}. Equivalently a law on vertices has E Z=x and the bound almost surely, with at most n+1 atoms existentially. The law may depend on P,A,x; it is not one distribution for every A. For each additional linear objective c there is a good vertex with c^T v<=c^T x, not an assertion that every atom of one unbiased law has that cost property.

Define universal radius b(P) as supremum over m,A,x of the least such exact-marginal bound. The candidate gives k(P)/2<=b(P)<=54k(P), with singleton zero. N689 already records the same qualitative bounded-exchange classification, with upper4096k^3+48k. This new source proposes an O(k) quantitative refinement and a normalized proof; it is not Astra's first such classification. Original N689 proof/status remains unchanged and unvalidated. Matroid base edges have length2, giving bound108 for arbitrary matroids; a Boolean measurement matrix of column sparsity Delta scales to108 sqrt(Delta). Graphic matroids give exact edge marginals on spanning trees under this normalized measurement contract, not a general all-cut thin-tree or operator-norm sparsification theorem.

For any face F, varying coordinates s(F)<=k dim(F), proved from a spanning selection of incident edge directions. In sign variables Q=2P-1 this gives tangent dimension>=s/k at a fractional relative-interior point. Retained affine rows, deleted coefficients and offsets preserve current discrepancy; full deletion cost is bounded independently of n. A nonnegative spectral potential plus diagonal deposit and a positive ridge is normalized at the anchor point. The resolvent congruence is a quadratic-form identity on the orthogonal complement, not a general pseudoinverse transformation rule. High normalized modes and positive curvature are charged before intersection with the actual face tangent space; no alignment with a cube face is assumed.

The complete codimension budget is223s/(256k), leaving33s/(256k)>0 feasible directions after large rows, binding barriers, high modes and curvature restrictions. Concave barriers preserve both signs of a feasible direction. The tilted potential (L-1)_+^3-eta||y||^2+tau c^T(y-y0) has negative second derivative at any entirely fractional minimizer, with L<=1 handled separately. Thus each compact global minimization freezes a coordinate; at most n stages suffice existentially. Linear tilts have no curvature cost. Finite-set separation as tau tends to zero gives exact marginals; an exposed maximal edge midpoint gives the lower k/2 bound. The spectral/retained-row ingredients are explicitly credited to recent discrepancy work, not independently invented here.

Those compact constrained minima are generally nonconvex. Counting stages does not bound computation. For rational A,x, exhaustive vertex enumeration and an LP can find a law; this is exponential in n. Once supplied, n+1 vertices and rational probabilities of polynomial encoding length are exactly checkable, but finding them remains costly. The source does not implement a rounder or prove a polynomial-time sampler. N692 separately claims a polynomial-bit independence-oracle construction at constant262336, with missing standalone artifacts and unreviewed proof; it neither proves construction at108 nor validates the new normalized argument. Its progress/reset ideas are a review target, not an imported theorem.

The producer's exact dimension arithmetic and160 resolvent/24 curvature tests concern local analytic consistency only. Intermediate scouting remarks about other conjectures are preserved as process data without promotion. Independent correctness, historical priority, efficient construction at the sharper bound and a fundamental new computational capability remain UNKNOWN. The precise constructive task must charge face recovery, near-binding barriers, small coefficients, rational precision resets and total progress.
